contract.maximum: Signed quotient goldBalance/goldCost, optionally signed quotient extraBalance/extraCost; signed minimum of quotients capped by stock (sign-extended16-bit) is stored in MaxQuantity. report.question: Original town and Hill Fort creature upgrade cost consumers, dynamic MA:C relationship and rounding
report.evidenceKind: Ordinary bounded offline static PE disassembly and supplied Pascal cross-check. REA unavailable previously diagnosed. No REA Evidence record or runtime execution.

observations.finding: Town and fort share helper54eb50. Each resource uses signed comparison targetCost>sourceCost. Positive difference is multiplied by supplied quantity using32-bit SUB/IMUL; otherwise output0. No refund for equal or cheaper target. Clamping happens on compared input costs BEFORE quantity multiplication, not after.

Seven resources0..6 only (gold6). Each call reads current table pointer6747b0 then current source and target descriptors. WoG bootstrap row redirects pointer to7d0c90, making costs exactly MA:C base7d0cb0+id*0x74+resource*4. No independent upgrade-price table/cache in helper.

Identified town upgrade payment and creature upgrade dialog use common helper without extra percentage/rabate. Payment recalculates costs before subtracting seven resources; source creature ID changes to target. Ordinary positive quantity therefore pays full positive price difference times stack size.

Human fort dialog reads source creature descriptor level+4. Level0 takes explicit free branch after upgrade existence test; zero-initialized entire cost vector is retained, including non-gold resources even with custom prices.

For source levels1..6, fort calculates complete stack difference first. Only gold is then stored as float32, loaded and multiplied by float32 coefficient indexed by source level:level1=.25,2=.50,3=.75,4/5/6=1.0. Final conversion uses truncation toward zero; non-gold resources retain full helper results.

Fort sums each stack cost into seven-resource total; successful payment uses cached per-stack costs and subtracts seven entries. Gold discount and truncation happen per stack, before summing fort total.

Identified Amethyst relocation writes expanded descriptor base10082ed8 to6747b0 and relocates MA:C cost base to that base+0x20. Thus this relocation preserves shared dynamic cost memory. Not a proof against later or different plugins.

Two additional direct callers528105/529336 use common helper then source-level gold multiplier. Selected regions do not bypass all resource costs forlevel0. Their full caller purpose and control flow are not reconstructed, so they must not be generalized as identical to human fort free branch.

inferences.finding: MA:C modifications affect recalculated town/fort upgrade costs through current source AND target prices. Applying rule113 only to recruitment display or scaling a precomputed upgrade-price difference can diverge when odd costs are halved separately.

For ordinary values exactly representable in float32, fort gold is trunc(max(targetGold-sourceGold,0)*quantity*levelCoefficient). Quantity multiplication precedes discount; do not truncate discounted unit price first. This formula omits intentionalint32/float32 edge behavior beyond ordinary values.
Fort-wide gold affordability totals sum already-truncated per-stack discounted costs; a single final discount/rounding over all stacks can diverge.
